title: Unbounded in-memory ConcurrentQueue grows forever from unauthenticated webhook posts
owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Steve Sanderson; component: WebhookClient/
rationale: Bounds the root cause (unbounded retention): AddNew trims the queue to MaxEntries=1000 via TryDequeue after each enqueue, and the endpoint rejects payloads over 64KB with 413 before AddNew (bounding retained memory at cap x max-payload). GetAll/enumeration unchanged (ConcurrentQueue enumerator is snapshot-safe). Residual: payload cap enforced only on the HTTP path; Kestrel-level rate limits remain infra.
variants_checked: Only growable in-process store in WebhookClient; the ConcurrentDictionary of subscriptions is subscriber-bounded and drained; RegisteredHooks fetches remotely per page.
bypass_considered: Flood path now bounded by retention and payload caps regardless of post rate; concurrent AddNew transiently self-corrects at cap.
test_note: HooksRepositoryCapsRetainedHooksAtMaxEntries enqueues 1001 and asserts exactly 1000 retained including the newest.
review_reason: Hunk 1 fixes the root cause in the function owning the queue; caller-side 413 guard bounds the second dimension; test mirrors existing MSTest style.
